easy.def: Odd and different from other people.
examples: The eccentric man wore a funny hat.
Her aunt is eccentric.
He is an eccentric artist.

more.def: Behaving in an odd or unusual way that is different from most people.
examples: The eccentric inventor wore a hat with a propeller.
Her aunt is eccentric and keeps a goat in the yard.
The eccentric professor wore two different socks every day.
His eccentricity was funny.
An odd eccentricity.
Her eccentricity is charming.

more.def: A strange or unusual habit that makes a person stand out.
examples: Wearing a hat indoors was his eccentricity.
His eccentricities made him a favorite character.
One of her eccentricities was collecting spoons.

easy.def: A spiny animal from Australia that eats ants.
examples: An echidna has spines.
The echidna eats ants.
I saw an echidna.

more.def: A small spiny animal of Australia with a long snout that lays eggs.
examples: An echidna rolled into a ball.
The echidna uses its long tongue to eat ants.
An echidna is covered in spines.

easy.def: A sound that comes back to you.
examples: I yelled in the cave and heard an echo.
The big empty room has an echo.
I love to hear my echo in the tunnel.

more.def: A sound you hear again because it bounces off a surface like a wall or cliff.
examples: We shouted across the canyon and listened for the echo.
The echo of footsteps filled the empty hallway.
Bats listen for echoes to find insects.
Bats use echolocation.
Echolocation uses sound.
Dolphins use echolocation.

more.def: A way of finding objects by sending out sounds and listening to the echoes.
examples: Bats use echolocation to find insects in the dark.
Dolphins use echolocation to find fish.
Echolocation helps animals see with sound.

easy.def: A long pastry filled with cream and covered in chocolate.
examples: An eclair is a pastry.
I ate an eclair.
The eclair has cream.

more.def: A long pastry filled with cream and covered with chocolate.
examples: I ate a cream-filled eclair.
The eclair was sweet and soft.
The bakery sells an eclair with chocolate on top.

easy.def: When the moon hides the sun for a short time.
examples: We saw an eclipse of the sun.
The eclipse made the sky dark.
The eclipse lasted a few minutes.

more.def: An event when the moon, the Earth or the sun blocks the light from another, so that part of the sky goes dark for a while.
examples: During the eclipse of the sun, the sky grew dark in the middle of the day.
We wore special glasses to watch the eclipse safely.
The moon turned red and dim during the eclipse.

easy.def: About how living things and nature fit together.
examples: An ecological study.
The ecological balance.
It is ecological.

more.def: Having to do with how living things relate to each other and to their surroundings.
examples: Scientists studied the ecological balance of the pond.
Pollution can cause ecological harm.
The park is an ecological treasure.

easy.def: A scientist who studies nature and living things together.
examples: The ecologist counted frogs by the river.
An ecologist studies nature.
She is an ecologist.

more.def: A scientist who studies how living things relate to each other and to their surroundings.
examples: The ecologist studied the pond.
An ecologist tracks how animals and plants depend on each other.
She is an ecologist who studies the forest.

easy.def: Having to do with money and business.
examples: It was an economic problem.
The town has economic needs.
Economic help came.

more.def: Having to do with money, business and how a country or town makes and spends what it needs.
examples: The new factory brought economic growth to the town.
The mayor talked about economic problems and how to solve them.
Farming is a big part of the country's economic life.
An economical car.
The economical meal.
It is economical.

more.def: Saving money or using little; not wasteful.
examples: An economical car saves on gas.
The soup was an economical meal.
It is economical to buy in bulk.

easy.def: The study of money, buying and selling.
examples: Economics is about money.
She studies economics.
Economics is a class.

more.def: The study of how people make, buy, sell and use money and goods.
examples: Economics teaches how prices work.
He studied economics in college.
Economics explains why things cost money.

easy.def: A person who studies money and business.
examples: An economist studies money.
The economist spoke.
She is an economist.

more.def: A person who studies how money, goods and jobs work in a country.
examples: The economist explained why prices went up.
An economist studies how people spend money.
She works as an economist for the bank.

easy.def: The way a place makes, buys and sells things.
examples: The town has a strong economy.
Farming helps the economy.
The economy needs workers.

more.def: The way a country or town makes, buys and sells goods and services, and how money moves around.
examples: Farming is a big part of the economy in our state.
When many shops open, the town's economy grows stronger.
Tourists who visit the beach help the local economy.

easy.def: All the plants, animals and land of one place, working together.
examples: A pond is an ecosystem.
The ecosystem is healthy.
Fish live in the ecosystem.

more.def: All the living things in an area and the way they depend on each other and their surroundings.
examples: A pond is a small ecosystem with plants, fish and insects.
Bees are an important part of the ecosystem.
Pollution can harm a whole ecosystem.
She was ecstatic.
I was ecstatic to win.
An ecstatic cheer.
She was ecstatic when she found out she had won the prize.
The ecstatic crowd cheered when the team scored.
I was ecstatic to see my cousin after a whole year.

easy.def: In a very, very happy way.
examples: She cheered ecstatically.
He jumped ecstatically.
They danced ecstatically.

more.def: In a way that shows you are extremely happy.
examples: She cheered ecstatically when her team won.
The puppy wagged its tail ecstatically.
The children danced ecstatically.
